name: Lacrimal Drainage System Anomaly of Genetic Origin

criteria.description: Presence of congenital obstruction or malformation of the lacrimal drainage system confirmed by clinical examination
Positive family history of lacrimal drainage anomalies or related genetic disorders
Radiologic or dacryocystography evidence of anatomical anomalies in the lacrimal drainage pathway
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with lacrimal system development
Exclusion of acquired causes such as trauma, infection, or neoplasm

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital lacrimal drainage obstruction or malformation confirmed clinically and by imaging, plus positive family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and genetic testing when available.

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent tearing from birth or early infancy
searchTerms: tear drainage obstruction present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Epiphora due to lacrimal drainage malformation
pathognomonic.notes: Overflow of tears caused by drainage anomaly
searchTerms: excessive tearing from blocked tear duct

pathognomonic.notes: Cystic swelling over lacrimal sac region

common.notes: Repeated infections of the lacrimal sac
Sticky eye discharge due to obstruction
searchTerms: pus discharge from tear duct opening

common.notes: Swelling around the eye related to obstruction

occasional.notes: Inflammation of conjunctiva secondary to tear stasis
Mild distortion from chronic cystic swelling
Occasional blurred vision due to tear film instability

rare.notes: Serious infection spreading beyond lacrimal sac

searchTerms: systemic infection originating from lacrimal area
spread of infection from eye drainage

rare.notes: Rare syndromic presentations with facial malformations

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during dacryocystitis episodes
Microbiological cultures from lacrimal sac discharge
imaging: Dacryocystography showing obstruction or malformation of lacrimal drainage
CT or MRI demonstrating lacrimal sac cysts or anatomical anomalies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes regulating lacrimal system embryogenesis (e.g., FGFR2, PAX6)
Familial inheritance patterns consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive transmission
other: Clinical observation of persistent epiphora and lacrimal sac swelling
Exclusion of acquired causes by history and examination

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, infection, or neoplasm
Acute onset with pain and erythema

redFlags: Rapidly progressive periorbital swelling with pain
Signs of orbital cellulitis or abscess formation
Systemic signs of sepsis or spreading infection
